items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## Problem

`GTPWeightCache` pins one buffer per cache key (shape, dtype, direction, chain) for the whole
run. On an Ultra rank at GTP 64 that is 217 buffers, 17 GB, although only the current layer, the
prefetched next layer and a little scratch are ever in flight: about 1 GB during the backward and
1.2 GB between steps. The forward buffers sit idle through the whole backward and optimizer step,
the backward buffers through the whole forward.

## What this PR does

Eager (non-CUDA-graph) chains stop pinning their buffers

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Add flint parser
items.author: justinchiu
items.summary: Adds a flint parser subclass to correctly handle replies missing `<think>` blocks, which current glm47 parser misclassifies as reasoning-only output.
items.body:
## Overview and claims

Flint assistant turns may not generate `<think></think>` blocks at all, particularly on swe trajectories.
This breaks existing parsers.

The current recipe's glm47 parser (#62938) starts every reply in reasoning, so a reply without `<think>` would only be reasoning without closing `</think>`.
Forcing `<think>` every turn would probably be ok, but the model was not trained this way.

We implement a fix by subclassing the glm47 parser, rather than a minimal patch that adds flags to make the think block optional in glm47. Only flint would use those flags, which is a wast

items.title: feat(kernel): vectorize output store in AWQ dequantize_weights kernel
items.author: YuvrajSinghBhadoria2
items.summary: This PR optimizes the CUDA kernel by vectorizing the output store operation.
items.body:
## Summary

This PR optimizes the CUDA  kernel () by vectorizing the output store operation.

## Problem

The kernel previously wrote each thread's 8 dequantized half-precision values as 8 separate scalar 2-byte stores, despite already holding them in a  register.

## Solution

Replace 8 scalar stores with a single 16-byte  store. The math is unchanged and output is bitwise identical.

## Changes

- Removed the unused  shared memory array and  pointer
- Replaced the loop of 8 scalar stores with a single  store

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Abort streaming input before the first chunk
items.author: wuyixuan123
items.summary: Fixes AsyncLLM.abort to cancel pending streaming-input sessions before the first chunk arrives, preventing hung input tasks and ensuring clean iterator termination.
items.body:
## Overview

Make `AsyncLLM.abort()` terminate streaming-input sessions that are still waiting for their first input chunk. The input task is cancelled and the output iterator finishes without yielding an output.

Addresses the explicit-abort case in [this comment on #57061](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57061#issuecomment-6310672263), rather than the original issue's cancellation-during-registration case.

## Claims

- An external or internal abort before the first chunk stops the input producer and wakes the output consumer, including when the producer task has not started.

items.author: xiaohaifeng1999

## Overview

Non-streaming Kimi K3 content leaked raw XTML control-marker fragments when generation was cut mid-marker (`max_tokens`); the streaming path already kept them out of content, so the two paths returned different content for the same output. Gives `_strip_response_content` the streaming path's holdback and first-close boundary. Fixes #63941.

## Claims

- Non-streaming and streaming now parse every prefix of a K3 turn identically: the in-tree sweeps cover four turn shapes exhaustively (967 cut positions + 967 delta-split positions) — 174 divergent cut positions pre-fix, 0 post-fix

## Overview

With decode context parallelism (DCP), a plain fp8 KV cache and an fp8 prefill query, the MLA chunked-context loop dequantizes each rank's cached rows to bf16, all-gathers the bf16 rows across the DCP group, and reorganizes them with a Python loop (one slice per request and rank, plus `torch.cat`). CSGMV LoRA kernels launch one program per segment and column tile. items.title: [Perf] kda: Write convolution output directly into contiguous QKV planes
items.author: BBuf
items.summary: KDA already computes packed Q/K/V convolution in one call. Its token-major output leaves the three channel slices non-contiguous, so the FlashInfer prefill path materializes three copies before consuming them.
items.body:
## Motivation

KDA already computes packed Q/K/V convolution in one call. Its token-major output leaves the three channel slices non-contiguous, so the FlashInfer prefill path materializes three copies before consuming them. At the GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 16K-token shape, those copies cost more than the convolution itself.

## Modifications

Add an optional split-output layout to the existing Triton convolution. The convolution stores directly into contiguous Q/K/V planes in one allocation, using the runtime total-token count as the plane pitch. Arithmetic and convolution-state updates are unchanged

items.title: [Perf][KV Offload] Keep offload event metadata out of the cyclic GC
items.author: jthomson04
items.summary: keeps one entry for every chunk resident in any offload tier, and each entry held three objects tracked by Python's cyclic GC. With a large secondary tier, these entries make up most of the EngineCore's long-lived heap, so every full collection pauses the sche…
items.body:
## Overview

`OffloadingEventsTracker` keeps one `_OffloadEventMetadata` entry for every chunk resident in any offload tier, and each entry held three objects tracked by Python's cyclic GC. With a large secondary tier, these entries make up most of the EngineCore's long-lived heap, so every full collection pauses the scheduler for over 100 ms. This PR keeps the entries out of the cyclic GC.

Not a duplicate. The only open PR touching this class is #63129 (draft). It fixes a separate correctness problem: metadata loss when an `OffloadKey` is reused. It doesn't change how entries are tracked.

items.summary: Attention-DP ranks step in lockstep, so a decode step waits for the slowest rank. On a disaggregated generation worker the slowest rank is set by two maxima: the most KV tokens on one rank, and the most requests on one rank.
items.body:
## Description

Attention-DP ranks step in lockstep, so a decode step waits for the slowest rank. On a disaggregated generation worker the slowest rank is set by two maxima: the most KV tokens on one rank, and the most requests on one rank. items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse MXFP8 activation quant into the 1x32 dot_scaled linear for M <= 16
items.author: RuibinCheung
items.summary: On gfx950, (1x32-scale MXFP8 dense layers: MiniMax-M3/M3.1, ModelOpt/INC MXFP8) runs a separate launch before every GEMM. For bf16 activations with 1-16 rows, this PR quantizes the activation inside the GEMM instead, so each such linear is one launch and the o…
items.body:
## Overview

On gfx950, `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` (1x32-scale MXFP8 dense layers: MiniMax-M3/M3.1, ModelOpt/INC MXFP8) runs a separate `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` launch before every `tl.dot_scaled` GEMM. For bf16 activations with 1-16 rows, this PR quantizes the activation inside the GEMM instead, so each such linear is one launch and the output is bit-identical. Fused: K <= 1024 for M <= 16, and K = 2048 for M <= 4.

The fused GEMM quantizes only `min(16, next_pow2(M))` activation rows per K step and repeats them to fill the 16-row MFMA tile; that keeps the per-N-tile quant cost proportion

items.title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Profile rejection sampling before sizing the KV cache
items.author: Alex-Wengg
items.summary: MRV2's KV cache profiling ignores spec-decode verification (rejection sampling), causing undersized cache; this PR runs the real rejection sampler during profiling to capture accurate memory peaks.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

MRV2's startup profiling runs only the regular sampler on one logits row per request, so it never measures spec-decode verification: logits for every draft position plus the bonus token, then rejection sampling. The KV cache is therefore sized from a peak verification exceeds. This runs the rejection sampler on a dummy batch with a full draft per request during profiling, as MRV1 does via `SpecDecodeMetadata.make_dummy`. Fixes #63942. MRV2 counterpart of the mrv1-only #46270.

## Validation

A6000, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, ngram drafter, `max_num_seqs=256`

items.body:
## Description

A `/v1/responses` request whose `web_search` tool asks for live results (any `external_web_access` other than `false`) is rejected with a 400 when this server cannot search. That happens when no provider is configured, and also when one is configured, because the search loop is not wired into this endpoint yet. The rejection is deliberate. An answer the model gave without the search the client asked for looks like any other answer, so the client cannot detect it. A 400 tells the client to drop the tool and retry.

Some clients attach the tool to every request and never drop it.

items.title: [Fix] hicache: Reject host mappings that exceed NUMA capacity
items.author: quaternior
items.summary: HiCache's host-wide budget can accept a buffer that cannot fit in the worker's permitted NUMA nodes. For example, a single rank can pass the global budget check for a 127 GiB buffer while bound to a node with about 126 GiB total RAM.
items.body:
## Motivation

HiCache's host-wide budget can accept a buffer that cannot fit in the worker's permitted NUMA nodes. For example, a single rank can pass the global budget check for a 127 GiB buffer while bound to a node with about 126 GiB total RAM.

This adds a physical-capacity check before the built-in mmap and SHM allocators create a new mapping. It catches an impossible pinned-buffer size early, with the requested size and permitted nodes in the error.

Related work:

## Motivation

Speculative target verify on GDN (gated delta rule) hybrid models snapshots the full
recurrent state after every draft step into `MambaPool.intermediate_ssm`, so that the
commit can copy back the state of the accepted step. The buffer is
`(max_running_requests + 1) x num_draft_tokens x state_size_per_layer x num_gdn_layers`
and is reserved for the whole lifetime of the server. For Qwen3.8-27B (48 GDN layers,
TP2) with DFLASH block 8 it is **3.66 GB per GPU at `--max-running-requests 12`**, taken
straight out of the KV pool, and it grows linearly with the concurrency cap.

items.author: okorzh-amd
items.summary: The paged MXFP4 sparse indexer (gfx950, #58671) fills the step's top-k rows with -1 before its top-k kernels run. On decode rows that go to vLLM's (gfx950 k = 512 path: #56743), the fill is dead: that kernel writes all k entries of every row.
items.body:
## Overview

The paged MXFP4 sparse indexer (gfx950, #58671) fills the step's top-k rows with -1 before its top-k kernels run. On decode rows that go to vLLM's `top_k_per_row_decode` (gfx950 k = 512 path: #56743), the fill is dead: that kernel writes all k entries of every row. This PR skips the fill on those rows, as the gfx942 indexer already does (#60731).

## Claims

- **Bit-exact by construction.** This is argued from the code and not yet checked on GPU. Below 128 rows and below k = 2048, every path of `top_k_per_row_decode` stores all k slots of each row, with -1 past a short row's end.

## Overview

GLM-4.5, GLM-4.6 and GLM-4.7 FP8 (160 routed experts, `moe_intermediate_size=1536`) at TP8 look up the fused MoE config `E=160,N=192,device_name=NVIDIA_H100_80GB_HBM3,dtype=fp8_w8a8.json`. vLLM ships this key for H200, B300 and MI350 but not for H100, so on H100 the Triton fused MoE uses the default config for every layer. items.author: MohitAMD
items.summary: Moves RDMA completion waits off the model forward thread in MoRIIO WRITE mode so transfer timeouts fail only the affected request instead of crashing the entire engine.

## Overview

In MoRIIO WRITE mode, the prefill can wait for a request's RDMA completion on the model forward thread (`wait_for_save` → `seal_pending_transfers` → `_finalize_if_complete`). A failed or timed-out transfer now sends `write_failed` to decode, so only that request fails.

## Claims

- A WRITE transfer that fails or times out no longer kills the prefill engine. It fails only its own request: decode reports it in `faile

When the last pipeline (or virtual pipeline) stage holds only MTP layers, its local decoder block spec is empty. items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Removes blocking host-wait during disaggregated decode by starting KV cache copies before batch admission and using non-blocking event checks across ranks for coordinated request scheduling.
items.body:
## Motivation

A PD decode with `--disaggregation-decode-host-receive-threshold` below 1 receives a request's KV cache into host memory and copies it to the device when the request joins a batch. The scheduler submitted that copy as the request was admitted and then called `finish_event.synchronize()`, so it waited for the in-flight forward and then for the copy while the forward stream idled. This PR removes that host wait: the copies start early, and a request joins a batch once its copy has finished on every rank that shares it.

## Motivation

DSV4.1 ratio-1/2 compressed KV pools can leave a substantial part of their memory budget unused. A multi-conversation working set can therefore spill to external storage unnecessarily.

items.author: phambinhfin
items.summary: On sliding-window attention layers, start the Triton prefix-prefill context loop at the first tile the window can reach instead of at tile zero. Everything before it is masked to and provably cannot affect the result.
items.body:
## Overview

On sliding-window attention layers, start the Triton prefix-prefill context loop at the first tile the window can reach instead of at tile zero. Everything before it is masked to `-inf` and provably cannot affect the result. Output is bit-identical, and one prefill call on a 32,000-token context is 14.6x faster on MI325X.

## Claims

- One prefix-prefill call is 3.8–15.0x faster on MI325X for contexts of 8,192–32,000 tokens against a 2,048-token window. Cost stops scaling with the prefix and tracks the window instead, flat at about 183 µs from 2,048 tokens upward.

items.author: LucasWilkinson

Once a P/D request (`do_remote_prefill`) arrives, an unpinned resident page stops being read immediately and its block returns to the pool only after the steps already scheduled have been processed. items.title: [Fix] diffusion/moss: Preserve full latents for sequence parallelism
items.author: BBuf
items.summary: MOSS-Image sequence parallelism currently shards image latents twice. The pipeline slices the latent height before the DiT builds full-image RoPE and independently shards the joint image/text tokens.
items.body:
## Motivation

MOSS-Image sequence parallelism currently shards image latents twice. The pipeline slices the latent height before the DiT builds full-image RoPE and independently shards the joint image/text tokens. On the tested 2048×2048 checkpoint, main SP2/SP8 produce repeated horizontal strips.

Keep the original latent at the pipeline boundary and let the DiT own sequence sharding/gathering. This restores correct multi-GPU scaling with four production lines and an extension to the existing distributed regression. No new flag, tensor copy, dependency or attention arithmetic is introduced.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Hold async KV loads into blocks an in-flight step reads
items.author: vMaroon
items.summary: Fixes KV cache corruption on HiSparse P/D decoders by deferring async NIXL page loads until the in-flight step reading that page completes.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes KV corruption on HiSparse P/D decoders: a NIXL load can overwrite a GPU page while the previous step is still reading it. The request that was reading it emits garbage for the rest of its output. The fix makes the scheduler start such a load one step later, once the step that reads the page is done.

Fixes #63811.

## When it happens

All four hold at once:

1. **HiSparse is on.** It returns a running request's clean resident pages to the GPU pool early; the request keeps reading them until the pool hands them out again.
2. **Async scheduling** (`max_concurrent_batches > 1`)

items.title: [Fix] scheduler: Skip --prefill-decode-interval when nothing is decoding
items.author: akhilg-nv
items.summary: holds back the next prefill for N scheduler rounds after each prefill batch, so requests that are already decoding get N decode steps in a row and keep a steady inter-token latency. The counter counts scheduler loop iterations, not decode steps.
items.body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

`--prefill-decode-interval N` holds back the next prefill for N scheduler rounds after each prefill batch, so requests that are already decoding get N decode steps in a row and keep a steady inter-token latency. The counter counts scheduler loop iterations, not decode steps. When no request is decoding, an iteration has nothing to run: it polls for new requests, does idle housekeeping, and goes round again. Chunked prefill splits a long prompt into chunks (8,192 tokens with `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`), and the scheduler treats each chunk as a prefill batch.

items.body:
## Motivation

DeepGEMM picks MegaMoE's BLOCK_M from the mean tokens per expert plus one sigma. Real decode routing is more skewed, so hot experts spill into a second M block that streams their weights again. Decode MegaMoE is bound by weight streaming, so that extra pass costs a full weight read. A larger BLOCK_M for decode-sized calls removes the extra pass.

## Modifications

- In decode and target-verify CUDA graphs, FP8xFP4 MegaMoE calls where DeepGEMM picks BLOCK_M 16 or 32 use 64, and calls where it picks 64 use 96. Larger choices are kept. `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_RAISE_DECODE_BLO
discussion: cc @kpham-sgl to review.

items.title: [Perf] paged-experts: fewer host syncs in host-planned steps
items.author: N3mezis
items.summary: Reduces host-GPU sync overhead in paged-experts MoE routing by batching state reads and slot map uploads into single copies, cutting idle GPU time during host-planned waves.
items.body:
# [Perf] paged-experts: fewer host syncs in host-planned steps

## Motivation

This PR aims to decrease TTFT.

Currently, Paged Experts (#42557) plans a step on the host when it routes more entries than the K resident slots: prefill, and decode batches past `K // top_k`. Such a step runs in waves, and each MoE layer syncs with the GPU 6 times plus once per wave (twice on the compacted Marlin path): two reads of the device LRU state, `torch.unique().tolist()`, a blocking upload of each wave's slot map, a `nonzero()` per compacted wave, `step.item()`, and two blocking uploads of the state back.

items.body:
## Description

MiniMax-M3's sparse indexer caches one 128-dim index key per token in each of its 57 sparse layers, and every TP rank keeps all of it. With FP8 index-K that is 7,296 B per token per GPU: 28% of a rank's KV bytes at TP2 and 44% at TP4/TP8.

## What does this PR do?

Previously, `fully_shard_context` was an alias for `FsdpContext`, coupling construction-scope management with runtime state that persists throughout training. These responsibilities have different reasons to change: construction controls which context new modules join, while runtime behavior controls communication streams and prefetching. Fixes #20965.

The Marlin NVFP4 MoE method reuses the CUTLASS loader, which packs FC1 as `[w3; w1]` (up first, gate second). `_apply_activation` took the first half as the gate, so SwiGLU/GeGLU experts computed `act(up) * gate`. items.title: [BUG] Vocab-parallel cross entropy returns 0 loss and 0 target gradient for confident tokens
items.author: mlzoo
items.summary: Fixes vocab-parallel cross entropy computing zero loss/gradients for confident tokens due to softmax denominator rounding in fp32.
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Once the target logit leads the logsumexp of the other logits by more than ~16.6 (the cross entropy is computed in fp32), `vocab_parallel_cross_entropy` and `fused_vocab_parallel_cross_entropy` return a loss of exactly 0 and a target gradient of exactly 0, while every other class keeps its positive gradient. The row gradient then sums to `+exp(-margin)` instead of 0.

items.author: zhaoyuanh-nvidia
items.summary: Aggregated Helix prefill runs the full prompt on every context-parallel (CP) rank for attention, but each rank must persist only the compressed MLA KV records in the cache pages it owns. Previously, prefill could write non-owned records into rank-local cache s…
items.body:
## Description

Aggregated Helix prefill runs the full prompt on every context-parallel (CP) rank for attention, but each rank must persist only the compressed MLA KV records in the cache pages it owns. Previously, prefill could write non-owned records into rank-local cache storage, so the cache was not a valid handoff to Helix decode.

This PR maps each new context token's global position to a rank-local KV slot using the Helix page ownership rule. A slot of `-1` suppresses the persistent KV and scale-cache writes on non-owning ranks. The existing MLA RoPE/append operator accepts these option

## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

items.title: fix: run dense fused kernels through the FSDP2 LM head
items.author: ZiyiXu06
items.summary: Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads, including models such as Qwen3. Previously, the fused forward accessed directly, bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular Tensors with DTensors during matrix multipl…
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

items.title: Fix YaRN cache reuse for shorter context-parallel sequences
items.author: Sunt-ing
items.summary: With context parallelism, running a shorter sequence after a longer one can reuse the wrong YaRN positions and change the model's output. The cache contains positions already split between CP ranks.
items.body:
- [X] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

With context parallelism, running a shorter sequence after a longer one can reuse the wrong YaRN positions and change the model's output. The cache contains positions already split between CP ranks. For CP2 rank 0, length 64 caches positions `0…15, 48…63`, but length 32 needs `0…7, 24…31`. Taking a prefix of the old cache gives the wrong positions.

Rebuild the cache when a non-packed sequence shrinks with CP > 1. CP1 and packed inputs can still reuse the cache.

…he actor and reference model

vLLM never samples some token ids (the out-of-tokenizer tail, plus the vision placeholders): it sets their logits to -inf before sampling. The actor and the reference model still compute probabilities over the full vocabulary, so the policy that is sampled from and the policy being trained differ. Nothing in training then keeps the actor's probability on those ids in check, and it can drift freely since they are never sampled and never penalized.

items.title: [MFSDP v2] Reuse local gradients across reduce-scatter windows
items.author: shjwudp
items.summary: Weight caching saves all-gathers but not reduce-scatters. Local gradient accumulation reduces the inner RS count from to at the cost of retaining full gradients for selected modules.
items.body:
## Design

Add opt-in `SchedulePolicy(reduce_scatter_interval=k)` to MFSDP v2. A module reuses one full local-gradient buffer per trainable parameter group, accumulates in main-gradient precision, and reduces every `k` completed backwards. The last microbatch flushes a shorter window; the default remains one reduction per backward.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

items.title: [vllm, rollout] fix: honor teacher temperature in on-policy distillation
items.author: yph22
items.summary: Honor when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation. Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

Fixes #8216

### What does this PR do?

`parallel_compute_score_async` in `PrimeRewardManager` had no branch for dict results, so dict-returning reward functions (math_dapo, rlla, ...) hit `float(result[0])`, raised `KeyError: 0`, and `verify()`'s except-all fallback silently zeroed the whole batch.

This adds the same `isinstance(result, dict) -> result["score"]` handling that `NaiveRewardManager` / `BatchRewardManager` / `DAPORewardManager` already have.

## Summary

This PR adds opt-in LoRA support for Megatron actor training in slime.
It freezes the base model and trains low-rank adapters for supported
dense projections, hybrid-attention projections, and MoE shared/routed
experts.

Rollout engines receive effective base-plus-adapter weights through the
existing full-weight synchronization path, without requiring native

items.author: LinzeShi
items.summary: If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach. This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. [Discussion: independent check on main: this no longer reproduces.]

### Bug Description

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. The expected behavior is to bound each probe, then check process liveness and retry while the process is alive. The overall startup wait should remain unbounded for slow model loading.

### Steps to Reproduce

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

## Background

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

A failure at any of those stages left already-created actors alive. Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to `_actor_handlers` only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Solution

- Register each actor immediately after creation, before rank-0 rendezvous lookup.

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.title: fix(rollout): support fan-out results in group reward models
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Those paths expect, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.
items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.title: fix(rm_hub): stop substring-matching gpqa letter labels and short answers
items.author: shaurya416
items.summary: Fixes #2409 ## Problem falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply.
items.body:
Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

items.author: tengeel

items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

items.body:
## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Fixes #1369.

`distributed_masked_whiten(..., shift_mean=False)` used to center, scale, then add the mean back:

```

items.author: yuyz-cyber

items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.title: require --ref-load when KL is enabled instead of crashing with a TypeError
items.author: rootkiller6788
items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.title: fix: preserve equals in extra environment values
items.author: imshunsuke
items.summary: For example: was parsed as: This corrupts padded or otherwise -containing environment values. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged.
items.body:
## Summary

- Preserve `=` characters after the first separator in the space-separated `extra_env_vars` fallback parser.
- Add regression coverage to the always-on CPU test matrix.

## Problem

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

`TOKEN=abc== END=ok`

was parsed as:

`{"TOKEN": "abc", "END": "ok"}`

This corrupts padded or otherwise `=`-containing environment values.

## Change

Use `split("=", 1)` so only the key/value separator is consumed. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged

## Background

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.

`sglang_url` points to the SGLang router address, but the router does not expose or forward the `/abort_request` endpoint.

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

## Motivation

`convert_torch_dist_to_hf.py` supports `--add-missing-from-origin-hf`, which restores tensors that are present in the original Hugging Face checkpoint but absent from the Megatron `torch_dist` checkpoint.

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

## Summary

This PR adds an optional rollout data transfer path for **disaggregated training** (separate rollout and actor GPUs). When enabled, vime transfers rollout tensors (`tokens`, `loss_masks`) through **Mooncake Store** instead of the Ray object store.

This is useful when rollout and training run on different GPUs or nodes and you want a dedicated high-bandwidth transfer layer rather than serializing large tensors through Ray.

Ported from [slime PR #1709](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/1709).

## What changed

- New `--transfer-backend` flag: `ray` (default) or `mooncak

items.summary: Replace the pause/resume-based rollout abort with a delete-type abort, so that under the long tail is truncated to partial (and resumable next step) instead of either deadlocking or running to completion.
items.body:
## What

Replace the pause/resume-based rollout abort with a **delete-type** abort, so that under `--partial-rollout` the long tail is **truncated to partial** (and resumable next step) instead of either deadlocking or running to completion.
